html:
The Amangu are an Aboriginal people of the mid west coast of Western Australia, around present day Geraldton and the Greenough and Irwin rivers. They are one of the Yamatji peoples of the region.

Their coast faces the Houtman Abrolhos islands, where the Dutch ship Batavia was wrecked in 1629. Their neighbours were the Nhanda to the north, the Badimaya inland and the Whadjuk and other Noongar peoples to the south.

Settlers moved into the area in the 1840s and 1850s, after lead and copper were found and sheep runs opened. Geraldton grew into a port on their land. The map shows the Amangu from 1600 to 1815. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
